title: Amul Named World's Strongest Dairy Brand as Indian Food Brands Hit $9.9 Billion
excerpt: Brand Finance's 2026 report ranks Amul first globally for dairy brand strength, with five Indian brands now commanding a combined $9.9 billion in brand value.
body:
• Amul has been crowned the world's strongest dairy brand with a Brand Strength Index score of 93 out of 100 and an AAA+ rating in Brand Finance's Food & Drinks 2026 report.
  • Five Indian brands — Amul, Mother Dairy, Britannia, Nandini, and Tata Consumer Products — now hold a combined brand value of $9.9 billion across global food and dairy rankings.
  • Amul's brand value surged 22% to $5 billion, making it the fourth most valuable dairy brand and 13th most valuable food brand worldwide.
  • The Gujarat-based cooperative has been expanding into US markets with fresh milk and dairy products, part of a push that now spans more than 50 countries.

India's flagship dairy cooperative has reached a milestone in global brand recognition. Gujarat Cooperative Milk Marketing Federation (GCMMF), which markets products under the Amul brand, has been named the world's strongest dairy brand in Brand Finance's Food & Drinks 2026 report, outpacing rivals that have long dominated international rankings.

Amul secured a Brand Strength Index (BSI) score of 93 out of 100 — the highest in the Dairy 10 category — earning it an elite AAA+ brand strength rating. The brand also climbed to second place among the world's strongest food brands overall, trailing only Brazil's Sadia.

A $5 Billion Brand Built on Cooperatives

Amul's brand value rose 22% year-on-year to $5 billion, placing it fourth among the world's most valuable dairy brands and 13th in the Food 100 list. It is the only Indian brand in the global top 50 food brands.

Brand Finance attributed the performance to Amul's farmer-owned cooperative model, which links 3.64 million milk producers across approximately 18,600 village cooperatives directly to consumers. The federation procures around 32 million litres of milk daily and recorded a turnover of ₹65,911 crore ($7.9 billion) in 2024-25, up from ₹59,545 crore the previous year.

"Amul's strength is built on decades of consumer trust, extensive distribution reach and a deep connection with households across the country."

— Brand Finance, Food & Drinks 2026 Report

The cooperative has also been climbing the Rabobank Annual Global Dairy Top 20, moving from 14th to 12th position in 2026, with an estimated dairy turnover of $8.4 billion.

Mother Dairy, Britannia, and Nandini Also Gain Ground

Amul was not the only Indian brand to post strong growth. Mother Dairy's brand value rose 22% to $1.4 billion, pushing it to 60th in the Food 100. The company's BSI score improved from 70.6 to 72.8, reflecting its push into value-added products like high-protein curd and paneer through its Pro range.

Britannia climbed to 63rd in the Food 100, with brand value up 17% to $1.3 billion and an AAA- brand strength rating. Brand Finance noted the company has maintained momentum through innovation within familiar categories, including launches like 50-50 Dipped and vegetarian cake variants.

Karnataka's Nandini, owned by the Karnataka Milk Federation, entered the rankings at 71st with a brand value of $1.1 billion, up 4%. Its partnership with IPL franchise Royal Challengers Bengaluru has given the regional brand broader national visibility, while new products like high-protein milk and probiotic curd have expanded its appeal.

Global Context and What's Next

Globally, Nestlé retained its position as the most valuable food brand at $24.6 billion, while Coca-Cola held the top non-alcoholic drinks spot despite a slight 1% decline to $46.1 billion. China's Yili continued as the most valuable dairy brand at $14.5 billion.

For diaspora consumers in the United States, Amul's international expansion is especially significant. The cooperative has been introducing fresh milk and dairy products in key US markets, with products now exported to more than 50 countries. That push, combined with nearly 100 new product launches this year spanning protein beverages, frozen foods, cookies, organic staples, and premium chocolates, positions Amul to compete not just on nostalgia but on product breadth.

The combined $9.9 billion brand value of India's top five food and dairy brands signals a broader shift: Indian food brands, long fixtures of domestic kitchens, are now earning the international rankings to match their scale.
nri_angle: Amul's expansion into key US markets brings familiar Indian dairy products closer to diaspora consumers, while the cooperative's global rise underscores the international clout of Indian food brands.
